A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ShapeDiscover research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across reorganization and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original topological-inference comparisons, neuroscience and visualization experiments, and runtime measurements in Section 5 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds component ablations, parameter sensitivity and noise experiments in Appendix I.9.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3 retains the same graph construction, spectral initialization, fuzzy-cover parametrization, losses and optimization procedure. The new ablation configurations and separate initialization subsection do not change the proposed default method.

E1.justification: The original datasets and tasks are retained. Figure 19 adds evaluation on additively corrupted 2-sphere and 3-sphere inputs, introducing noisy-input scenarios within the existing synthetic-data coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same Rips, Alpha and Witness variants, and the visualization experiments retain their Mapper and UMAP comparators. Newly discussed coarse-graining methods are not added to the experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark settings and metrics remain unchanged. The added analyses introduce component-removal and random-initialization controls, parameter grids over cover size, neighborhood size and regularization, and a normalized additive-noise protocol in Figures 18–19.

E4.justification: v1 includes timing with and without topology loss and a discussion of geometry-loss redundancy. v2 substantially extends this evidence with four-dataset loss and initialization ablations in Table 5, parameter sensitivity in Figure 18, and noise robustness in Figure 19.

E5.justification: v1 does not report repeated-run uncertainty. v2 Figure 19 explicitly reports means and standard deviations over 10 runs per noise level. This establishes new uncertainty reporting, not an increase in runs for the retained benchmarks.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their entries, but Table 5 and Figures 18–19 add substantial diagnostic results. Removing either measure or regularization loss gives zero recovery on all four ablation datasets. MNIST depictions in Figures 4 and 15 are also replaced by six-element displays, while Figure 4 retains inconsistent references to vertex I and ten nonempty elements.

T1.justification: New Appendix C derives computational time and space bounds, including the cost of zero-dimensional persistence and total optimization. The main loss theorem, its proofs, and the existing nerve and regularization arguments remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and four principal contributions retain their meaning. Section 6 replaces the broad statement that the algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art methods with the more qualified claim that cover learning can improve the two principal TDA methodologies by addressing specific shortcomings.

C2.justification: Table 5 substantially qualifies the account of what drives performance: measure and regularization losses are essential in the tested settings, clustering initialization matters especially on real data, and topology loss helps chiefly with random initialization. Section 6 consequently suggests simplifying the pipeline and develops additional applications to vectorization and persistence-based clustering.

D1.justification: Figures 18–19 document parameter-sweep values, unit-hypercube normalization and coordinate-wise uniform noise for the added experiments. Existing implementation dependencies, hardware, default training settings, code-access information and runtime entries are retained. The relationship between noise level and perturbation amplitude is not fully specified.

R1.justification: New Appendix E substantially broadens positioning through comparisons with diffusion coarse-graining, Reeb-graph methods and PAGA, citing Brugnone, Huguet, Pascucci and Wolf and colleagues. Section 6 adds connections to density- and persistence-based clustering; the introductory application citations are also revised.

P1.justification: v2 introduces a fuller numbered subsection hierarchy, separates initialization, clarifies notation and clustering relationships, and expands the conclusion. The main narrative order and much of the prose remain intact. Some references newly mislabel existing definitions and lemmas as theorems.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5 and Figures 18–19, replaces the MNIST panels in Figures 4 and 15, and relocates several retained displays. Most existing visual material and table structures remain unchanged. The revised MNIST images are not accompanied by a consistent Figure 4 caption.

improvement.justification: The new ablations and sensitivity studies improve understanding of component necessity and operating limits, while Appendix C clarifies computational scaling. These benefits are partly offset by the unexplained MNIST replacements and stale caption, which weaken that qualitative example, and incomplete noise-protocol details. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
